A real bug was found and fixed before any result was kept: the first prompt version leaked the real predicted value directly into the instruction and the JSON answer example, so the model just echoed it back (spurious 16/16 SUPPORTED). Fixed by never mentioning the real value; regression-guarded by test_predicted_object_is_never_present_in_the_prompt. Real result after the fix (llama3.2:latest, corpus v0.2, 2026-09-17): 16/16 CONTRADICTED -- a genuine empirical finding (the small local model lacks a basis to answer correctly for several of these subjects, e.g. Alice never appears as a MERE_DE source in discovery_facts) not a mechanism defect. Live-LLM results are not pinned to an exact value anywhere (non-deterministic across runs/models/hardware, unlike every deterministic M6 mechanism); tests/test_m7_live_ollama_demo_v0_1.py asserts only guaranteed structural properties and skips cleanly when Ollama is unreachable, keeping the main suite portable. See MetaHIA_M7_LLM_Fact_Proposer_V0_1.md.
m7_lan_fallback_2026-09-17: Configured at explicit user request: local Ollama (LOCAL_HOST/LOCAL_MODEL) as primary, LAN sandbox server (192.168.1.11:11434, model qwen2.5-coder:7b, consistent with this project's established WP18 local-model precedent) as fallback -- triggers only on genuine unreachability, never on a merely-unusable-but-reachable response. Network endpoint choice only, no code dependency on llm/ollama_backend.py. Two real bugs found and fixed before keeping this: (1) the first live fallback attempt timed out at 30s on a cold model load on the shared LAN server (network itself was 78ms) -- fixed with a longer fallback_timeout=90s; (2) after a successful fallback, LLMProposal.model still named the requested primary model rather than the one that actually answered -- fixed by having ollama_generate_json_with_fallback() return (response, model_used) instead of a bare dict, verified end to end with local genuinely stopped. Also fixed the live demo test's reachability probe, which was using a full /api/generate call (needs a loaded model) with only 5s timeout -- switched to the lightweight /api/tags endpoint. 356/356 tests passing, zero regression. See MetaHIA_M7_LLM_Fact_Proposer_V0_1.md Sec.5.

m6_hash_integrity_incident_2026-09-17: A genuinely external reviewer running the delivered zip package (commit 613c4cd) found m6_corpus_from_m4_m5_v0_1.py's actual hash (d78ebf1b...) did not match the frozen f075f730... in the M6 v0.1 protocol. No test outcome was affected (purely additive change), but hash integrity was genuinely broken. All 13 hashes across both M6 protocols re-verified individually after the fix. A second, independently environmented reviewer (Python 3.11.2 / pytest 7.2.1) then confirmed 338/338. See JOURNAL_DE_BORD.md for the full chronology.

m7_mixed_corpus_promotion_2026-09-18: Answers the load-bearing question raised before choosing the next M7 step (over length>1 extension or third-party validation): does feeding M7's LLM evidence into the SAME M6 promotion pipeline as the adversarial-corpus evidence help, hurt, or leave holdout calibration unchanged? m7_corpus_mixed_v0_1.py unions m6_corpus_from_m4_m5_v0_2.build_real_corpus_v2() (26 records, GROUNDED_DIRECT) with m7_corpus_from_llm_v0_1.build_llm_witnessed_corpus() (16 records, GROUNDED_ANALOGY, all still 16/16 CONTRADICTED as in the 2026-09-17 result) into one combined corpus fed unchanged through split_by_rule/StructuralLearningPolicy/evaluate_promotion. Fairness verified: the LLM mechanism can only add records for rules already present in the adversarial corpus, so split_by_rule assigns the identical holdout rule set under the same seed in both runs -- a genuine same-holdout comparison. Real result (llama3.2:latest, seed=0, brier_threshold=0.5): baseline (adversarial only) holdout Brier=0.48125/ECE=0.025, train=16/holdout=5, PROMOTE; mixed (adversarial+LLM) holdout Brier=0.47/ECE=0.025, train=25/holdout=8, PROMOTE. Honest reading: the Brier movement (0.48125->0.47) is small on a 5-8 record holdout and cannot be credited to genuine LLM analogical skill given its evidence is itself systematically CONTRADICTED regardless of ground truth -- conclusion is calibration-NEUTRAL at current scale/model, not a demonstrated improvement, and does not yet justify further investment (length>1 extension, third-party validation) ahead of improving the LLM's individual accuracy or growing the corpus. See MetaHIA_M7_LLM_Fact_Proposer_V0_1.md Sec.6. 364/364 tests passing, zero regression.
